claim: The final SMB v2 run reconciles 1152 unique tuples, 384 degradation traces, 64 independent works, six conditions and three methods.
scope_limitations: Applies only to the fresh measurable-staff-scale SMB v2 sample; v1 is development/stress evidence.

claim: EDSR and SwinIR improve both primary fidelity metrics over bicubic in all six conditions at source-level paired 95 percent intervals.
scope_limitations: Statistical separation does not establish practical relevance, musical correctness, real-scan transfer or population prevalence.

claim: SwinIR leads EDSR on both primary metrics in x2-clean, x2-moderate and x4-clean, but EDSR is favored on at least SSIM-Y in the three remaining conditions.
scope_limitations: Two PSNR comparisons cross zero; method preference is conditional and tied to the retained runtime and qualitative evidence.

claim: The fixed qualitative cases contain altered symbols, text or digit corruption, and natural-image texture even when aggregate fidelity improves.
scope_limitations: Six outcome-independent pages and 18 assessments are descriptive cases, not defect prevalence or a blinded specialist study.

claim: EDSR is the default fidelity-cost option for assisted visual enhancement; SwinIR is reserved for conditions where its paired gain justifies the extra runtime.
scope_limitations: The original must be retained and outputs human-verified; no semantic restoration, OMR, archival replacement or autonomous publication claim is supported.

claim: The bounded EDSR adaptation run reconciles 360 unique tuples, 24 paired bootstrap rows, 30 fixed qualitative PNGs, two checkpoints and source-disjoint 45/13/20 project roles.
scope_limitations: Roles are project-defined inside SMB's official test split; the primary 64-work benchmark is excluded and remains separate.

claim: SMB-adapted EDSR improves PSNR-Y and SSIM-Y over the official pretrained EDSR in all six conditions at source-level paired 95 percent intervals.
scope_limitations: Twenty fresh works; matched synthetic degradations and within-SMB adaptation only; no musical-correctness, real-scan, other-corpus or deployment claim.

claim: The fixed student review classifies four of six adapted EDSR cases as improvement without a clear new defect and two strong cases as LR damage not recovered; no case is classified as introduced or amplified damage.
scope_limitations: Six descriptive cases do not estimate prevalence or semantic correctness; the strong cases retain losses in small symbols, text, digits and fine geometry.
